title: Variable Flexibility - Case and Spacing Revisited
description: Learn that BOTH keywords AND variable names are case-insensitive in Robot Framework.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Remember how keywords are case-insensitive? Here's the secret: variable names are ALSO case-insensitive! Let me prove it to you."
story.context: Robot Framework normalizes EVERYTHING—both keywords (Log, Set Variable) AND variable names (${myVar}, ${MyVar}, ${MYVAR}) are all treated the same. This complete flexibility makes Robot Framework truly human-friendly.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "See? Robot Framework is consistently flexible. BOTH keywords and variables are normalized. No distinction—everything is case-insensitive!"

instructions: Create a test case named 'Variable Flexibility Demo'
- Use 'Set Variable' (standard) to create ${test1} with value 'Standard keyword'
- Use 'set variable' (lowercase) to create ${test2} with value 'Lowercase keyword'
- Use 'SET VARIABLE' (uppercase) to create ${test3} with value 'Uppercase keyword'
- Use 'SeT VaRiAbLe' (mixed) to create ${test4} with value 'Mixed case keyword'
- Reassign ${STATUS} with value 'ALL SYSTEMS GO' (same variable!)
Log all three status variable variations to show they display the SAME value (last assignment wins)
Add comment explaining the key rule: BOTH keywords and variables are case-insensitive
hints: Keywords ARE case-insensitive: Log = log = LOG
Set Variable = set variable = SET VARIABLE = SeT VaRiAbLe
${myVar} and ${MyVar} are THE SAME variable (normalized internally)
Robot Framework normalizes both keywords AND variable names
Use comments with # to explain the rule
solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Variable Flexibility Demo
    # Keywords are case-insensitive
    ${test1}    Set Variable    Standard keyword
    ${test2}    set variable    Lowercase keyword
    ${test3}    SET VARIABLE    Uppercase keyword
    ${test4}    SeT VaRiAbLe    Mixed case keyword
    Log    All four tests created successfully
    
    # Variable NAMES are ALSO case-insensitive!
    ${status}    Set Variable    system online
    ${Status}    Set Variable    SYSTEM READY
    ${STATUS}    Set Variable    ALL SYSTEMS GO
    Log    ${status}    # Shows: ALL SYSTEMS GO (last assignment wins)
    Log    ${Status}    # Shows: ALL SYSTEMS GO (same variable)
    Log    ${STATUS}    # Shows: ALL SYSTEMS GO (same variable)
    
    # KEY RULE: BOTH keywords AND variables are case-insensitive!

theory.title: Variable Flexibility: Everything is Case-Insensitive in Robot Framework
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 brings up a holographic display showing multiple code variations all working identically.

"PROTO-7, many developers believe variable names are case-sensitive. They're WRONG. Just like keywords, variable names are also case-insensitive and spacing-flexible. Let me show you the truth."

The Complete Truth

Syntax Flexibility in Robot Framework

  • ✅ KEYWORDS are CASE-INSENSITIVE & SPACING-FLEXIBLE
    • Log = log = LOG = L o G
    • Set Variable = set variable = SET VARIABLE = SeT··VaRiAbLe
    • Create List = CREATE LIST = create··list
  • ✅ VARIABLE NAMES are ALSO CASE-INSENSITIVE & SPACING-FLEXIBLE
    • ${myVar} = ${MyVar} = ${MYVAR} = ${my_var} = ${m y v a r}
    • ${status} = ${Status} = ${STATUS} = ${s t a t u s}
    • @{items} = @{Items} = @{ITEMS} = @{i t e m s}

Why This Matters

Robot Framework normalizes BOTH keywords and variable names internally. This gives you complete flexibility in how you write your tests.

The Revelation

*** Test Cases ***
Flexibility Demo
    ${userName}    Set Variable    Alice
    Log            ${username}              # ✅ WORKS! Same variable!
    Log            ${USERNAME}              # ✅ WORKS! Same variable!
    Log            ${user_name}             # ✅ WORKS! Same variable!
    Log            ${u s e r n a m e}       # ✅ WORKS! Same variable!
    
    # All access THE SAME variable - "Alice"

How Normalization Works

Robot Framework normalizes BOTH keywords and variables by:

  1. Converting to lowercase
  2. Removing spaces, underscores, and hyphens

So ${MyVariable}, ${my_variable}, ${MYVARIABLE}, and ${m y v a r i a b l e} all become ${myvariable} internally.

Keyword Flexibility (Review)

All of these are identical:

*** Test Cases ***
Keyword Variations
    ${x}    Set Variable    A        # Standard
    ${y}    set variable    B        # Lowercase
    ${z}    SET VARIABLE    C        # Uppercase
    ${w}    SeT VaRiAbLe    D        # Mixed
    
    Log    ${x}                      # Standard
    log    ${y}                      # Lowercase
    LOG    ${z}                      # Uppercase
    LoG    ${w}                      # Mixed
    
    # All work perfectly! Keywords are normalized.

Variable Name Flexibility (The Truth!)

Variable names are ALSO normalized—Robot Framework treats these as the SAME variable:

*** Test Cases ***
Variable Flexibility
    ${status}    Set Variable    FIRST
    ${Status}    Set Variable    SECOND
    ${STATUS}    Set Variable    THIRD
    
    Log    ${status}     # Output: THIRD (last assignment)
    Log    ${Status}     # Output: THIRD (same variable)
    Log    ${STATUS}     # Output: THIRD (same variable)
    
    # These are THE SAME VARIABLE!
    # Each assignment overwrites the previous one!

Practical Examples

*** Test Cases ***
Real World Usage
    # Create variable with one case
    ${api_url}    Set Variable    https://example.com
    
    # Access with different cases - ALL WORK!
    Log    ${API_URL}      # ✅ https://example.com
    Log    ${ApiUrl}       # ✅ https://example.com
    Log    ${a p i u r l}  # ✅ https://example.com
    
    # Reassign with different case
    ${API_URL}    Set Variable    https://production.com
    
    # ALL variations now show new value
    Log    ${api_url}      # ✅ https://production.com
    Log    ${ApiUrl}       # ✅ https://production.com

Why This Design?

AspectCase-Insensitive KeywordsCase-Insensitive Variables
Reason Natural language readability Consistency and flexibility
Benefit Write keywords naturally Access variables without remembering exact case
Philosophy Human-friendly automation Same normalization everywhere

Best Practices

1. Pick ONE Naming Convention and Stick to It

*** Variables ***
# Recommended: snake_case for readability
${api_url}         https://example.com
${max_retries}     3
${timeout_ms}      5000

# Also valid: camelCase
${apiUrl}          https://example.com
${maxRetries}      3

# Avoid: Mixed styles (confusing)
${API_url}         # ❌ Inconsistent
${Max_Retries}     # ❌ Inconsistent

2. Use Consistent Casing for Readability

While Robot Framework treats ${myVar} and ${MYVAR} as the same, humans need consistency to read code easily.

3. Understand the Normalization

Both keywords and variables are normalized:

  • Log To Console → logtoconsole
  • ${My_Variable} → ${myvariable}

This is why Log = log and ${Var} = ${var}.

What IS Case-Sensitive?

Important exceptions where case DOES matter:

  • Dictionary keys: ${dict}[Name] ≠ ${dict}[name] (string keys in dictionaries)
  • File paths: On Linux/Mac, File.txt ≠ file.txt
  • String comparisons: Should Be Equal compares "Robot" ≠ "robot" (unless using case-insensitive comparison)

Testing Your Understanding

*** Test Cases ***
Quiz: What Happens?
    ${Count}    Set Variable    5
    log         The count is ${count}
    
    # Answer: ✅ WORKS PERFECTLY!
    # Why: 'log' (keyword) works (case-insensitive)
    #      ${count} = ${Count} (variables also case-insensitive)

Common Misconception Debunked

MYTH: "Keywords are flexible, but variable names are strict."

TRUTH: "Both keywords AND variable names are flexible—Robot Framework normalizes everything!"

Mnemonic to Remember

"Robot Framework is consistently flexible—EVERYTHING is normalized."

  • Keywords: Case-insensitive, spacing-flexible ✅
  • Variables: Case-insensitive, spacing-flexible ✅
  • Dictionary keys: Case-sensitive (exception) ⚠️

MENTOR-9: "Demonstrate the truth. Use Set Variable in multiple cases (lowercase, uppercase, mixed) to show keywords are flexible. Then create ${status} and later access it as ${Status} and ${STATUS} to prove they're THE SAME variable. Show the last assignment wins!"
